record.title: BootLoops manuscript reports 15 new Feynman-integral results among 30 computed integrals
record.summary: A preliminary author-hosted manuscript presents analytic forms or differential equations with boundary data and standalone evaluation code for 30 multi-loop Feynman integrals across polylogarithmic, elliptic, and K3/Calabi–Yau classes. The authors identify 15 as known results recomputed by the method and 15 as new at the kinematics stated in each entry. The claimed set includes results for exact-top-mass diboson processes and massive three-loop light-by-light integrals, but several are restricted to fixed mass ratios, kinematic slices or paths, and one W-pair result is evaluated on an unphysical line.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report analytic or differential-equation results for 30 multi-loop Feynman integrals: 15 known results recomputed and 15 described as new at the stated kinematics.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The manuscript says each computed result is accompanied by standalone evaluation code and is checked against independent numerical values at kinematic points not used in fitting or boundary data; it states a threshold of at least 30 digits. This review did not execute the code or reproduce the checks.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper says a large language model operated the BootLoops toolkit for the computations; the guest post identifies the work as Matthew Schwartz’s independent project rather than an Anthropic research result.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The public repository README describes the code as written by Claude under Matthew Schwartz’s direction, says Schwartz maintains the project and that it is not an officially supported Anthropic product, while the license notice carries a 2026 Anthropic, PBC copyright attribution. These statements distinguish maintenance/support from the copyright line.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent group reproduced the new integral results or checked the paper’s standalone evaluation code during this review.
The claim of novelty is the authors’ literature assessment, and several results apply only at a fixed mass ratio, slice, path, or unphysical line.

brief.importance_rationale: If independently validated and extended to useful physical kinematics, new analytic multi-loop integrals can change the tools available for precision collider predictions, a material but specialized research consequence. The current paper is preliminary and several results have narrow kinematic domains, so this is not a general prediction-performance claim.
limitations: The source is an author-hosted preliminary manuscript, not independently peer reviewed in this review.
Novelty is reported by the author and was not independently adjudicated.
The stated 30-digit criterion and comparisons are manuscript-reported; no code was run here.
Several results have restricted kinematic domains; this does not establish general physical-region coverage.
No measured improvement in collider observables, turnaround time, or experimental prediction accuracy is reported.
LLM contribution is author-reported and does not establish autonomous scientific discovery.

The repository README says Matthew Schwartz maintains BootLoops and it is not officially supported by Anthropic, while its license notice carries an Anthropic, PBC copyright line; these distinct provenance statements should not be collapsed into a claim of Anthropic-led research.
brief.summary: A preliminary author-hosted manuscript presents analytic forms or differential equations with boundary data and standalone evaluation code for 30 multi-loop Feynman integrals across polylogarithmic, elliptic, and K3/Calabi–Yau classes. The authors identify 15 as known results recomputed by the method and 15 as new at the kinematics stated in each entry. The claimed set includes results for exact-top-mass diboson processes and massive three-loop light-by-light integrals, but several are restricted to fixed mass ratios, kinematic slices or paths, and one W-pair result is evaluated on an unphysical line.

technical.claimed_result: Thirty multi-loop integrals across polylogarithmic, elliptic and K3/Calabi–Yau classes are presented; 15 are reproductions of known results and 15 are claimed new at the stated kinematics.
technical.demonstrated_result: No independent numerical result was established in this review. The manuscript reports analytic expressions or differential equations, boundary data, evaluation code and independent-point numerical comparisons.
technical.implementation_status: Author-hosted preliminary manuscript and public toolkit documentation are accessible; no independent adoption or measured downstream collider use is established.
technical.mechanism: A hybrid bootstrap combines analytic constraints on the function space with high-precision numerical integration and coefficient reconstruction; where a finite function basis is inadequate, the paper solves differential equations and transports boundary data.
technical.novelty: The authors describe 15 of 30 entries as new at the stated kinematics; this review did not adjudicate priority independently.
technical.regime: Specific integral families and kinematic domains in the paper’s Table 1 and entries; some results are fixed mass points/ratios, selected slices or paths, and the nonplanar W-pair result is on one unphysical kinematic line.
technical.reproducibility: The manuscript links standalone evaluation code and a BootLoops toolkit. This review inspected the PDF and toolkit documentation, but did not download/run the repository or independently reproduce any result.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares each result with prior published analytic results where known and with auxiliary-mass-flow numerical values at selected independent points; no broad model or collider-prediction benchmark is reported.

brief.title: BootLoops manuscript reports 15 new Feynman-integral results among 30 computed integrals
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported expressions and checks hold, adding reusable analytic representations for previously untreated multi-loop integrals can reduce a technical bottleneck in precision collider calculations. The result is a methods and integral-coverage advance; the manuscript does not establish an improvement in measured collider predictions or broad physical impact.
